supersedes: The stage0-gate blockingCondition, which recorded item 1 as NOT CAPTURED. It is captured here.

instrument.renderer: Blender EEVEE via Blender MCP, headful, addon blender_mcp_pinned on port 9876
instrument.fovRationale: Matched to Cesium's default PerspectiveFrustum fov so the screen-pixel arithmetic below is the arithmetic of the shipped viewport rather than of a render setting.
instrument.viewTransform: Standard (no filmic curve): tone must read as authored.
instrument.light: One sun, 3.0 W/m2, 52 deg elevation, 35 deg azimuth. Identical for every variant.
instrument.camera: Fixed ground azimuth 35 deg, elevation 12 deg, aimed at the asset's bounding-box centre, at the stated distance. Identical for every variant of a building.
instrument.cropMethod: Blender render border with crop-to-border: a TRUE 1:1 crop of the same camera, not a zoom. A pixel in a crop is a screen pixel.
instrument.cropAlignment: The crop box is computed ONCE from lod_0 and reused for all three variants, so the three crops are pixel-aligned.
instrument.instrumentDefectFound: The first implementation derived the crop box per variant and produced 201x162 against 200x161 for the same building, silently comparing misaligned rows. Fixed before any number below was taken.
instrument.blenderIncidentAvoided: The scene was cleared by deleting objects and purging orphans. read_factory_settings(use_empty=True) was never called; it unregisters the MCP addon and was what terminated the previous attempt.

variants.lod0: The shipped lod_0 GLB, textured, exactly as retained.
variants.lod1: The shipped lod_1 GLB, untextured, exactly as retained.
variants.lod0flat: THE RECONCILIATION PREVIEW. lod_0 geometry with the image unbound and each material's baseColorFactor multiplied by its own tile's mean texel. It is what a tone-reconciled level looks like: no image, no TEXCOORD, tone preserved. Built by material edit in Blender; nothing was re-emitted.

metricDefinition.toneMeanAbs: Mean of the per-channel MEAN difference over the building's pixels. A whole-surface, low-spatial-frequency shift.
metricDefinition.toneChannelSpread: max minus min of the three per-channel means. NON-ZERO MEANS A HUE ERROR: a grayscale tile can only move all three channels together.
metricDefinition.patternRms: RMS of the difference AFTER the per-channel mean is removed. High-spatial-frequency structure only.
metricDefinition.whyDecomposed: A flat-tone variant slightly off in overall brightness would otherwise inflate the tile-detail figure with what is really a tone residual. Removing the mean makes the pattern number a statement about spatial structure, which is what 'is the tile visible' asks.

screenPixelArithmetic.seamRationaleVerdict: CONFIRMED, with a wide margin. The emission seam (midtown-core-v3-materialization.ts:920-923) argues a 128-pixel joint is below a screen pixel beyond 250 m. At 350 m one screen pixel spans 12.8 to 44.9 texels; even at 120 m it spans 4.4 to 15.4. The joint is sub-pixel at BOTH distances tested.

findings.theAnswer: TONE. At mid distance the visible difference between the two levels is a tone and hue discontinuity, not missing tile detail.
findings.theDecisiveFrame: lod0flat -- lod_0 with the tile REMOVED but its mean tone preserved -- is very close to shipped lod_0 at 350 m, while shipped lod_1 is visibly bleached and cooler. Removing the tile entirely costs almost nothing if the tone is kept; keeping only the flat palette costs a lot.
findings.whyTheNumbersAloneMislead: patternRms (0.030-0.039) and toneMeanAbs (0.020-0.041) are the same ORDER, which on the numbers alone reads as a tie. It is not a tie perceptually: the tone term is a whole-surface shift the eye reads instantly, while the pattern term is high-frequency structure already at or below the pixel grid. The stills are the evidence for that, and they are committed.
findings.hueErrorConfirmedInARender: CONFIRMED, and its distribution is more careful than a first pass suggested. toneChannelSpread on the two limestone-bearing buildings is 0.0158/0.0181 (doitt:131170) and 0.0163/0.0265 (doitt:778052), blue consistently the largest gap: lod_1 is brighter AND cooler. On the two DECIMATED brick-bearing buildings it is 0.0003-0.0016, i.e. no measurable hue error. But the FALLBACK building doitt:1302589 is brick-bearing and shows 0.0082/0.0169 -- and it is the one comparison holding geometry CONSTANT. So the honest reading is NOT 'limestone only': decimation averages the two levels' facades differently and masks the hue gap, and the cleanest isolation available shows it on a brick building too. The Stage 0 analytic finding of a 12.3% per-channel ratio spread is confirmed; its per-class distribution is not settled by five buildings.
findings.fallbackPair: doitt:1302589 has lod_1 emitted as FULL GEOMETRY, so its lod_0/lod_1 comparison holds geometry constant and is the cleanest isolation of the palette gap available: toneMeanAbs 0.0199 at 350 m and 0.0406 at 120 m, channel spread 0.0082 and 0.0169, lod_1 again brighter and cooler.

limitations: FIVE buildings, not a population. Class coverage is met (brick 3, curtain 5, spandrel 5, limestone 2) but this is a stratified sample and nothing here is a distribution.

The lod0flat variant for the fallback building doitt:1302589 was a NO-OP: the flatten found no image-bound material to convert, so its tileDetail row is null rather than zero-by-measurement. That building contributes a tone reading only.
lod0flat is rendered on lod_0 GEOMETRY. A truly rescoped lod_1 would carry lod_1 geometry with reconciled tone; the render shows the tone remedy, not the final artifact.

The tile mean used for lod0flat is the raw texel mean the committed class-tile-luminance record states. A residual whole-surface brightness offset of 1.4-3.7% remains between lod0 and lod0flat, which is why the pattern term is reported mean-removed.
EEVEE is not the shipped renderer. CesiumJS draws the app. What transfers is the geometry of the comparison and the pixel arithmetic, not an absolute appearance claim.

The hue error's dependence on texture class is NOT settled here. Two decimated brick buildings show none and the one geometry-constant brick building shows some, which means decimation is a confound this sample cannot separate from class.
claim: A stratified five-building, two-distance, three-variant rendered comparison, taken through Blender MCP against the retained -c1 bytes. It answers the question the Stage 0 gate was blocked on. It is not a population measurement and it is not an acceptance of any release.
